questions.question: The number of boundary conditions required to solve the differential equation [latex]\frac{\partial^2 \phi }{\partial x^2}+\frac{\partial^2 \phi }{\partial y^2}=0[/latex] is
Value of the integral [latex]I=\int_{0}^{\pi /4}cos^{2}xdx[/latex] is
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} I&=\int_{0}^{\pi /4}\cos ^{2}xdx \\  &=\int_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{1+\cos 2x}{2}dx \\  &=\int_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{dX}{2}+\int_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{\cos 2x}{2}dx \\  &=\frac{1}{2}\left [ x \right ]_{0}^{\pi /4}+\frac{1}{2}\left [ \frac{\sin 2x}{2} \right ]_{0}^{\pi /4} \\  &=\frac{\pi }{8}+\frac{1}{4}\left [ \sin \frac{\pi }{2}-\sin x \right ] \\  &=\frac{\pi }{8}+\frac{1}{4}\times 1 =\frac{\pi }{8}+\frac{1}{4} \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html: [latex]\begin{aligned} I&=\int_{0}^{\pi /4}\cos ^{2}xdx \\  &=\int_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{1+\cos 2x}{2}dx \\  &=\int_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{dX}{2}+\int_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{\cos 2x}{2}dx \\  &=\frac{1}{2}\left [ x \right ]_{0}^{\pi /4}+\frac{1}{2}\left [ \frac{\sin 2x}{2} \right ]_{0}^{\pi /4} \\  &=\frac{\pi }{8}+\frac{1}{4}\left [ \sin \frac{\pi }{2}-\sin x \right ] \\  &=\frac{\pi }{8}+\frac{1}{4}\times 1 =\frac{\pi }{8}+\frac{1}{4} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question:
The solution for the following differential equation with boundary conditions
y(0)=2 and y'(1)=-3 is [latex]\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}=3x-2[/latex]
questions.explanation: [latex]  \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{3x^{2}}{2}-2x+C_{1}[/latex] Integrating, we get, [latex] \begin{aligned}  y&=\frac{3x^{3}}{6}-\frac{2x^{2}}{2}+C_{1}x+C_{2} \\ \therefore  \;\; y\left ( 0 \right )&=2=0+10+C_{2} \\  C_{2}&=2\\ \text{Again }  -3&=\frac{3}{2}\left ( 1 \right )^{2}-2\left ( 1 \right )+C_{1} \\  -3&=1.5-2+C_{1}\\ C_{1}&=-3+0.5 \\&=-2.5=-\frac{5}{2} \\   y&=\frac{x^{3}}{2}-x^{2}-\frac{5}{2}x+2\end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
[latex] \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{3x^{2}}{2}-2x+C_{1}[/latex]
Integrating, we get,
[latex] \begin{aligned} y&=\frac{3x^{3}}{6}-\frac{2x^{2}}{2}+C_{1}x+C_{2} \\ \therefore \;\; y\left ( 0 \right )&=2=0+10+C_{2} \\ C_{2}&=2\\ \text{Again } -3&=\frac{3}{2}\left ( 1 \right )^{2}-2\left ( 1 \right )+C_{1} \\ -3&=1.5-2+C_{1}\\ C_{1}&=-3+0.5 \\&=-2.5=-\frac{5}{2} \\ y&=\frac{x^{3}}{2}-x^{2}-\frac{5}{2}x+2\end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question:
Consider the following two statements related to reinforced concrete design, and identify whether they are TRUE of FALSE: I. Curtailment of bars in the flexural tension zone in beams reduces the shear
strength at the cut-off locations. II. When a rectangular column section is subject to biaxially eccentric
compression, the neutral axis will be parallel to the resultant axis of bending.

options.A: Both statements I and II are TRUE
options.B: Statement I is TRUE, and statement II is FALSE
options.C: Statement I is FALSE, and statement II is TRUE
options.D: Both Statements I and II are FALSE

questions.explanation: Statement I: Curtailment of bars in the flexural tension zone in beams reduces the shear strength at the cut-off locations. This statement is TRUE because cutting tensile reinforcement decreases dowel action and reduces shear resistance at that location. Statement II: When a rectangular column is subjected to biaxially eccentric compression, the neutral axis will be parallel to the resultant axis of bending. This statement is FALSE because for biaxial bending, the neutral axis is governed by the interaction: [latex] M_x y + M_y x = 0 [/latex] The slope of the neutral axis is: [latex]\text{slope of N.A.} = -\frac{M_y}{M_x} [/latex] Whereas the resultant bending axis has slope: [latex]\text{slope of resultant moment axis} =\frac{M_y}{M_x} [/latex] Thus, they are not parallel.
questions.topic: Shear, Torsion, Bond, Anchorage and Development Length
questions.explanation_html:
Statement I: Curtailment of bars in the flexural tension zone in beams reduces the shear strength at the cut-off locations.
This statement is TRUE because cutting tensile reinforcement decreases dowel action and reduces shear resistance at that location.

Statement II: When a rectangular column is subjected to biaxially eccentric compression, the neutral axis will be parallel to the resultant axis of bending.
This statement is FALSE because for biaxial bending, the neutral axis is governed by the interaction:
[latex] M_x y + M_y x = 0 [/latex]
The slope of the neutral axis is:
[latex]\text{slope of N.A.} = -\frac{M_y}{M_x} [/latex]
Whereas the resultant bending axis has slope:
[latex]\text{slope of resultant moment axis} =\frac{M_y}{M_x} [/latex]
Thus, they are not parallel.
